lead.title: Berlin Heals implants first patient in C-MIC IV, the first double-blind, sham-controlled trial of its cardiac microcurrent therapy
lead.deck: The Zug-based medtech announced on November 18 the first implant in the international C-MIC IV trial, performed at the university hospital in Kragujevac, Serbia: 60 heart failure patients with reduced ejection fraction, randomized 1:1 to active microcurrent or a switched-off device, across six European countries including Spain, Belgium, the Netherlands and Denmark. Because patients cannot feel the current, blinding is complete — higher-grade evidence meant to set up the pivotal US IDE study, the company's real value catalyst.

milestone.title: Lille medtech Lifebloom starts producing its Oxilio wheelchair-exoskeleton, already ordered by some twenty hospitals
milestone.summary: CE-marked Oxilio is a wheelchair that turns into a walking-assistance exoskeleton: it supports up to 80% of the patient's weight and brings them back to a seated position if they lose balance. The first 120 units are coming off the Villeneuve-d'Ascq line, funded by an €8M raise in early 2026; Lille University Hospital and the hospitals of Gonesse, Laval and Tulle are among the first customers.
milestone.why: Moving from prototype to series production is where many rehabilitation medtechs fail; Lifebloom tackles it with firm orders and a target of more than 100 facilities within two years. The next step — home-use reimbursement, still to be built — will decide the real size of the market.

deal.thesis: Eight months after a $230M Series C, Science raises $400M (Khosla Ventures, 885 Capital, Tenet Healthcare, Y Combinator…) to roll out PRIMA in Europe — the retinal implant that came with its acquisition of France's Pixium, CE-marked in July: national reimbursement applications filed, first sites activated, first commercial implant expected in Germany. The thesis: Europe as the first commercial market for a brain-computer interface, ahead of FDA approval via the HDE pathway.

brefsEurope.title: Nyxoah wins default decision against Inspire at the Unified Patent Court
brefsEurope.summary: The UPC's Munich division issued a default decision on November 18 in favor of the Belgian medtech, which develops hypoglossal nerve stimulation for sleep apnea, in its European patent infringement action against US market leader Inspire Medical Systems. An interim win in a patent war fought on both sides of the Atlantic, with stakes for access to the European market.

brefsEurope.title: Percisio takes the podium at the MEDICA Start-up Competition with radiation-free navigation
brefsEurope.summary: Incubated at Paris Biotech Santé, the startup finished third in the November 17 final in Düsseldorf with a portable system that overlays 3D anatomy during interventional radiology procedures, with no additional radiation. The competition was won by Exalt, a Medical University of Vienna spin-off that tests how a patient's cancer cells respond to more than 100 drugs, ahead of Germany's Paracly (device cybersecurity).

brefsIntl.title: Masimo wins 510(k) for smartSedLine, the next generation of its anesthesia-depth monitor
brefsIntl.summary: The new module and EEG sensor carry an enhanced Patient State Index algorithm, faster at induction and more stable when EEG power is low. It is the seventh FDA clearance of the year for Masimo, now a Danaher company: intraoperative brain monitoring is becoming a consolidation play for large groups.

brefsIntl.title: MedInTech raises $25.7M Series C to move from robotic endoscopy into surgery
brefsIntl.summary: The round, co-led by Atinum Investment and KB Investment, will broaden its AI-assisted robotic endoscope range and take it into therapeutic and surgical applications. An Asian comparable worth tracking for Europe's endoluminal robotics players.

brefsIntl.title: Fziomed secures 510(k) for Dynavisc, an absorbable tendon-protection gel
brefsIntl.summary: The synthetic gel, applied after tendon repair to keep tissues apart during healing, has been sold outside the US for more than a decade (over 50,000 patients). A textbook case of the "Europe first, FDA later" path for biomaterials.

word.definition: A system that overlays the patient's 3D imaging and the path of the surgeon's instruments directly in their field of view (headset, glasses or tablet), letting them "see through" the skin during the procedure.

parts.label: Preoperative imaging
parts.role: the map (CT, MRI or ultrasound rebuilt in 3D)

parts.label: Optical or electromagnetic tracking
parts.role: the GPS (position of patient and instruments)

how.t: The software aligns the 3D model from imaging with the patient's actual anatomy on the operating table.
Cameras or sensors follow the patient and instruments in real time so the overlay stays accurate as everything moves.
The surgeon sees hidden anatomy and the ideal trajectory right on the surgical field, without looking away to a remote screen.

word.why: Conventional navigation relies on large, fixed, expensive stations; AR promises portable, cheaper guidance with no additional radiation, reaching operating rooms and departments that never had it. The FDA lists more than 100 authorized AR/VR devices, mostly via 510(k), and new reimbursement codes for navigation open up a business model: favorable ground for capital-efficient startups against the navigation giants.
